Input: the held impact review is support.review_sim.impact_sim (research work held by the real receiver, its review queued) instead of a bare_engine with an autospec store and synthetic waiting and review records; the review runs as a model call and ends for real, and the producer's sealed bytes become unreadable during the review's call because its accepted receipt no longer matches them, instead of a patched read_sealed_submission that always failed. read_sealed_submission and _hold_unreadable_impact_submission are observed with ObservedCalls instead of replaced. The legacy assert_called_once counted the reads of the second retry only; the new test compares every sealed read of the owner pass, in order: the review's input read of the producer (before the call), the receiver's read of the review's own output, and the retry's one read of the producer after the review ended, then one hold.

Input: the owner's formal check runs on a Sim whose active environment adopts the installed Lean by control (support.knowledge_installed_lean.adopt_installed: the toolchain is registered and moved to, the instance configures no Lean command and the host port finds the installed one) and whose Lean seam starts it as a real process, instead of _formal on knowledge_fixtures.formal_boundary_engine with autospec collaborators and a patched governance.authorize. The configured command (None) differs from the approved command, as the legacy fixture's 'unapproved-config-command' did (K-42), while the profile's pinned command is the discovered, approved one (execution_profiles._lean_contract), so an owner that handed the verifier the configured command would not verify: with that mutant (machine_invocation's lean_command replaced by the configured command) all four tests of this class fail. The legacy verifier Mock is engine_lifecycle.recorded_verifier, which runs verify_lean with jobs=sim.ports.jobs: the Lean worker's Job is the Jobs port fake instead of the real WindowsJob the legacy verifier (jobs=None) used; verify_lean in real Jobs is run by boundary.test_knowledge_formal_consumer.InstalledCompilerTests and boundary.test_knowledge_lean_verifier. This test asserts the K-42 split explicitly: the configured command is None, the verifier received the approved command and the one started Lean process is that command. _start_identity_review and _settle_activity, autospec doubles in the legacy fixture, run for real and are observed with ObservedCalls. The added Sim test fixes the product rule the configuration relies on: with a configured command other than the approved one the owner holds the formal check ('profile command differs from the approved trust environment') and starts no Lean.

Input: the partial result is the owner's real application of a split research response (its output bundle accepted, its insight bundle returned because the insight's evidence source changed during the call) instead of engine_fixtures.routing_engine with an autospec ResearchRepository, a maintenance submission and an autospec _apply_submission_bundles returning a fixed partial result; _record_task_receipt is observed with ObservedCalls instead of replaced.
